name: quadruped_control_abstract
source: Abstract—T his article considers quadruped locomotion control in the presence of uncertainties. Two types of structured uncertainties are considered, namely, uncertain friction constraints and uncertain model dynamics. Then, a min-max optimization model is formulated based on robust optimization, and a robust min-max model predictive controller is proposed by recurrently solving the optimization model. We prove that the min-max optimization model is equivalent to a convex quadratic constrained quadratic program by exploiting the structure of uncertainties. Moreover, a two-stage optimization algorithm is proposed to solve the optimization problem efficiently, allowing for the deployment of the controller onto the real robot. The results show that the proposed optimization algorithm can improve solving frequency by ~11x compared with Gurobi. The proposed controller is able to stabilize quadruped locomotion in challenging scenarios where the uncertainties are caused by significant disturbances and unknown environments.

name: quadruped_robot_introduction
source: This ability motivates a lot of work to develop quadruped robots, such as ANY mal [1], HyQ [2], MIT Cheetah [3], Cheetah II [4] and III [5], and Mini Cheetah [6], from the robotics research community, and Boston Dynamics Spot [7] and Unitree Al [8] from the commercial robot companies. However, it remains challenging to control quadruped robots to achieve agile and robust locomotion similar to their animal counterparts. In particular, the uncertainty in the robot model and the external environment places one of the key challenges for the controller design. It is critical to ensure stability and safety in scenarios with significant disturbances and prevent hardware damage from failures.

name: robust_mpc_computational_challenges
source: authors’ knowledge, this is the first time a robust min-max model predictive controller has been deployed on a legged robot in the real world. In the legged locomotion community, it is a recognized challenge [13], [17], because the robust min-max model predictive controller could be very computationally intense even in a small predictive horizon. Moreover, due to its potential conservativeness, it is usually impossible to apply the controller to real robots. By leveraging duality theory, convex analysis, active set method, and other optimization techniques, we tackle this challenge in a systematical way, and the experimental results show that the control performance is improved compared with the baseline controller. In what follows, we give a brief review of the related work and remark on the differences between the existing methods and this work.

name: quadruped_related_work
source: 1) Quadruped Locomotion Control: Following the pioneering work on the classic heuristic controller [19], many modelbased locomotion controllers are proposed for quadruped robots [20], [21], [22], [23], [24]. Recently, the quadruped locomotion community has seen an increasing number of works based on MPC [13], [14], [25], [26]. For example, Grandia et al.[13] presented a whole-body MPC approach based on differential dynamic programming (DDP) to address the latency problem of nominal MPC algorithms. A convex model predictive control (CMPC) method is proposed in [14] based on a linearized single rigid body model for MIT Cheetah 3, and can stabilize common quadrupedal gaits. It is further improved in [25] by incorporating whole-body control to achieve highly dynamic locomotion for MIT mini Cheetah.
